title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Box
providers.scope_notes: Do not substitute Box Shield location/anomaly detection or corporate firewall allowlisting for API source-IP enforcement.

controls.name: Disable unpublished platform apps by default
controls.what: Unpublished custom apps (OAuth and server-auth) are disabled until an admin enables them.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Enterprise Settings > Platform Apps
controls.quote: When you select Disable unpublished platform apps by default, Box disables all unpublished platform apps by default.

controls.name: Enable/disable user authentication app
controls.what: Admins enable or disable a custom OAuth 2.0 app for the enterprise by Client ID.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > User Authentication Apps
controls.quote: enable custom user authentication applications, such as OAuth 2.0 apps, and

controls.name: Integration Availability Status
controls.what: Disables a published integration for all or selected users; existing installs stop working.
controls.quote: If you disable an application on this page, account holders are unable to add the application to their Box accounts, and cannot use the application if the account holder previously installed it.

controls.name: Enable Integrations by default
controls.what: Toggling off disables all published integrations by default.
controls.quote: Integrations are enabled by default. When you toggle off Enable Integrations by default, Box disables all Integrations.

controls_unknown: No admin setting found that blocks developers from generating developer tokens; tokens expire after 60 minutes and inherit the app's scopes and the user's access.
Whether Box offers API source-IP enforcement for app tokens (no admin doc found; Shield/firewall not counted).
Whether new Limited Access (App Token) apps can still be created.
Whether Box SSO requirements constrain OAuth token issuance for managed users (not checked).
Whether app access level (App only vs App + Enterprise) and scopes can be overridden by the admin at authorization time; docs show them set by the developer in the Developer Console.

authentication.summary: OAuth bearer; server authentication via Client Credentials Grant or signed JWT, usually using an app service account.

federation.details: Box JWT auth is app-key authentication. Box token downscoping exchanges an existing Box token, not an arbitrary external IdP token.

ip_restriction.boundary: Box support docs refer to an enterprise 'IP Allowlist' setting turned on per enterprise (not a plan feature). Its coverage of API calls with this credential is not documented; confirm with Box.

renewal.summary: Refresh token lasts 60 days and is single use.

administration.summary: App scopes/access levels, administrator authorization, service-account/user access, token revocation and downscoped access tokens.
administration.conditions: Do not substitute Box Shield location/anomaly detection or corporate firewall allowlisting for API source-IP enforcement.

sso.details: OAuth sign-in goes through the enterprise SSO screen, but under SSO Required existing tokens are not revoked and keep refreshing.

offboard.details: Box support says making the user inactive (or revoking tokens) is how to stop the user's tokens.

inventory.details: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > User Authentication Apps lists apps and enablement state, not per-user tokens.

sso.ui: Admin Console > Enterprise Settings > User Settings > Enable Single Sign-On (SSO) for All Users > SSO Required

expiry.api: Fixed 60 min; read expires_in in the POST https://api.box.com/oauth2/token response

reads.ui: Admin Console > Reports > Create Report > User Activity; filter Action types to Downloaded

offboard.ui: Admin Console > Users and Groups > Managed Users > (user) > Edit User Account Details > Status: Inactive

token_format.notes: Opaque bearer access_token (expires_in ~3600s) plus single-use refresh_token valid 60 days. No documented prefix; not in GitHub secret scanning patterns.

log_sources.name: Box Enterprise Events (GET /events, stream_type=admin_logs / admin_logs_streaming)
log_sources.notes: Admin/co-admin with reporting permission. admin_logs: 1 year history; admin_logs_streaming: ~2 weeks live. Admin Console reports: 7 years.

log_sources.name: Box Shield alerts (SHIELD_ALERT in enterprise events)
log_sources.notes: Shield add-on only. Suspicious location/session, anomalous download alerts with ip_info and service_name.

credential_id_fields.notes: User mini object (id, name, login) acting; id 2 = Unknown User
User session; not populated on all events
Event-specific details ('how a user performed an event'); per-event keys not fully documented

lifecycle_events.notes: Login from a device not seen before
File accessed by user or programmatically by a Box application
Box invalidated a user session associated with an app
Failed interactive login (not API token failures)

anomaly_cues: USER_AUTHENTICATE_OAUTH2_ACCESS_TOKEN_CREATE for a user right after ADD_LOGIN_ACTIVITY_DEVICE from a new IP
Bulk DOWNLOAD/CONTENT_ACCESS by a user whose interactive LOGIN came from a different country or ASN
Token creates for a user shortly after FAILED_LOGIN bursts (consent phishing after credential stuffing)
Activity continuing after the user is deactivated or after OAUTH2_*_REVOKE
Shield SHIELD_ALERT suspicious session/location tied to the same user

containment.steps: POST /oauth2/revoke with client_id, client_secret and the access or refresh token; admin can disable the user-auth app in Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps.
containment.notes: Revoke acts on the presented token; whether other tokens the same user granted the app are killed, and whether disabling the app ends live tokens, is not documented.

sample_query.purpose: Pull OAuth token grants and new-device logins for 30 days to spot unexpected app consents

unknown: Field naming the OAuth client_id/app on token-create and use events
Whether app disable invalidates already-issued tokens

calls.reveals: the authenticated user (OAuth: the user who authorized the app)
calls.log_notes: Enterprise events feed exists but docs do not state whether this read produces an event

calls.reveals: items (files, folders, web links) under the account root (id 0); walk the tree
calls.rate_limit: 1000 API requests/minute per user; limit max 1000 items/page
calls.log_notes: Reads: docs do not state whether folder listing produces an enterprise event
Enterprise events (GET /events stream_type=admin_logs) list 'Downloaded'; 1yr historical, 2wk streaming, 7yr via Admin Console reports

calls.reveals: download_url + status_url for a single zip of many files/folders
calls.log_notes: Underlying file fetches may log as DOWNLOAD; a distinct zip event is not documented

unknown: Whether folder-listing and GET /users/me reads produce enterprise events
Whether POST /zip_downloads produces a distinct event vs per-file DOWNLOAD
